question: What is the total length (in km) of National Waterway-2?
solution:
The correct answer is __**891**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway-2 (NW-2)** is a significant inland water transport route in India, specifically located on the **Brahmaputra River** in the state of **Assam**.
 
• The total length of this waterway is **891 km**, stretching between **Sadiya** in the east and **Dhubri** in the west, near the international border with **Bangladesh**.
 
• It was officially declared as a National Waterway by the Government of India in the year **1988** to promote freight and passenger movement in the **North-Eastern Region**.
 
• This waterway provides essential connectivity for trade and commerce, linking major towns like **Dibrugarh**, **Neamati**, **Tezpur**, and **Guwahati (Pandu port)**.
 
• The management and development of **National Waterway-2** are handled by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**, which maintains a navigable channel for vessels throughout the year.
 
• It is an integral part of the **Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route**, allowing transit of goods between mainland India and the Northeast through **Bangladesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Waterway-1 (NW-1)**:

 
 
• This is the **longest waterway** in India with a total length of **1620 km**.
 
• It covers the **Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly** river system and connects **Prayagraj** in **Uttar Pradesh** to **Haldia** in **West Bengal**.
 
• It passes through the states of **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **Jharkhand**, and **West Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway-3 (NW-3)**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **West Coast Canal**, it spans **205 km** in the state of **Kerala**.
 
• It connects **Kottapuram** to **Kollam** and includes the **Udyogmandal** and **Champakara** canals.
 
• It was declared as a National Waterway in the year **1993**.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway-4 (NW-4)**:
 
 
• This waterway covers a length of approximately **1095 km**, involving the **Krishna** and **Godavari** rivers along with the **Buckingham Canal**.
 
• It traverses the states of **Andhra Pradesh**, **Tamil Nadu**, and the Union Territory of **Puducherry**.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway-5 (NW-5)**:
 
 
• With a length of about **623 km**, it includes the **Brahmani River**, **East Coast Canal**, and the **Matair River**.
 
• It primarily serves the industrial belts of **Odisha** and parts of **West Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**:
 
 
• The **IWAI** was established on **27 October 1986** under the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways**.
 
• Its **headquarters** are located in **Noida**, **Uttar Pradesh**, with regional offices in places like **Patna**, **Kolkata**, **Guwahati**, and **Kochi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Waterways Act, 2016**: The Government of India enacted this law to declare **106 new National Waterways** in addition to the existing **5**, bringing the total number of National Waterways to **111**.
 
• The development of these waterways is part of the **Sagarmala Project**, which aims to modernize India's ports and utilize its **7,500 km** coastline and **14,500 km** of potentially navigable waterways.
 
• Water transport is considered the most **fuel-efficient** and **environmentally friendly** mode of transport compared to road and rail, significantly reducing the **logistics cost** in the country.
